checkpointHistory.scope: Both hosted source runtimes passed the legacy seed 3/3, first process 13/13 and restart 6/6. All 31 native inputs matched raw Git bytes, clean and unchanged. Portable archives were built and read back; their executable workflows were not qualified at this revision.

Linux passed the legacy seed and ten first-process checks, then the bridge fixture failed because its non-isolated native background rejected unconditional contextBridge installation. Windows failed the real ASAR nested-path readback contract before Electron execution. Neither platform reached packaged execution.

Both source applications passed 3/3 legacy-seed, 14/14 first-process and 7/7 restart checks, including all twelve then-current bridge subchecks. Both overall jobs failed before packaged execution because npm 10 left empty top-level dependency scope directories in the copied production staging tree. The subsequent repair removed only those empty staging shells, without weakening file or byte verification.

Both actual packaged first processes passed 10/10 checks, including the two public HTTPS documents and integrated local-data forms. Both overall gates failed at restart comparison. URL-only readiness had accepted a different already-open duplicate before the selected tab committed. The Windows failed second-phase NetLog is incomplete JSON, so its complete traffic counts remain unknown.

The selected-target readiness correction passed the packaged first-process workflows on both platforms, but both restart comparisons still failed. Renderer window.close() bypassed the preventable native window-close path used for the final session snapshot. The later harness requests the ordinary PID-bound OS window protocol and verifies actual saved bytes before the next launch; it does not add an application save backdoor.
Last verified published source and actual packaged-executable workflows; finite acceptance of the recorded generated and public-page cases only.
